//: The engine wasm's split modules (docs/web-export.md §Modules): each module takes the functions whose demangled path, from its first non-std crate on, matches one of its patterns; the first module that matches wins. scripts/wasm-split.ts keeps in the primary every function a game using none of them runs (wasm-profile.ts) and every function `roots` reach up to `entries`, so such a game loads none.
//siblings: Modules built from one source per variant (og-physics' rigid/sim.rs, for dim2 and for dim3), whose identical bodies the linker folds under one name: a function one calls in the other goes to their parent (wasm-split.ts keepShared).
//roots: The engine's calls every game makes whatever it uses (scripts/wasm-split.ts framePath): a frame, a canvas attach, a geometry. Every function they reach by direct calls stays in the primary, stopping at `entries`.
//entries: The calls those make into a module only once the game uses it, each guarded in og-runtime (names without crate hashes): og.motion once og.MotionAgent is registered (engine/tick.rs render); set_mesh for a dynamic geometry's update, a streamed model's proxy and a destructible's hulls (generated geometry goes to physics' mesh source, bind/modules.rs note_mesh); the physics debug view; a video's stream once a video plays; og-runtime's terrain extraction, release, seabed and drop shadows once a terrain is loaded or named (present/extract/frame.rs uses_terrain, world/assets/release.rs). og-render makes its 3D world renderers through closures the frame path does not follow (renderer/resources.rs OnDemand).
